facts.text: Whitehall was incorporated as a village in 1947 and grew into a city during the 1950s as development accelerated.
The National Road, a historic U.S. highway, once ran through Whitehall, linking the city to early frontier routes.
In 1948, Whitehall opened the first shopping center strip in the country, called Casto's Town and Country, pioneering suburban retail.
The Lustron Home, a rare prefabricated steel house, sits at the south end of Whitehall Community Park and serves as the historical society headquarters.
Whitehall’s borders expanded east in 1952 to include the country club and Big Walnut Creek, defining its modern eastern edge.
The township originally named Truro was renamed Whitehall after an inn/tavern that gave the area its name in the early 1800s.
